text: One day. <break time="0.8s" /> An elder sister came from town. <break time="0.8s" /> To visit her younger sister. <break time="0.8s" /> Who lived in a village with her husband. <break time="0.8s" /> Drinking tea together. <break time="0.8s" /> The elder sister began to boast about the town. <break time="0.8s" /> Where people dressed well and ate fine food. <break time="0.8s" /> The younger sister did not like this. <break time="0.8s" /> And she said that she would never change her life. <break time="0.8s" /> For her sisters. <break time="0.8s" /> Our life may be rough. <break time="0.8s" /> But we are never anxious. <break time="0.8s" /> And we always have enough to eat. <break time="0.8s" /> She said proudly. <break time="0.8s" /> You town people may be rich today. <break time="0.8s" /> But tomorrow you could lose everything. <break time="0.8s" /> And end up on the street. <break time="0.8s" /> The elder sister laughed and answered that peasants lived in dirt all their lives. <break time="0.8s" /> And died in it, too. <break time="0.8s" /> Pahom, the master of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Was lying on top of the stove. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he listened to the womens talk. <break time="0.8s" /> It is true. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> We peasants are too busy with our work. <break time="0.8s" /> To think of any nonsense. <break time="0.8s" /> Our only trouble is that we have too little land. <break time="0.8s" /> And if I had plenty of land. <break time="0.8s" /> I would not fear the Devil himself. <break time="0.8s" /> The Devil who had been sitting behind the stove. <break time="0.8s" /> Heard everything. <break time="0.8s" /> And decided to give Pahom land. <break time="0.8s" /> And to trap him through it.
